html:
A Swiss and German Protestant mission whose first members reached the Gold Coast in 1828 and, after many deaths from fever, set up at Akropong in the Akuapem hills in 1835.

In 1843 it brought Christian settlers from Jamaica to help. Its missionaries, with African assistants, wrote down Twi and Ga, translated the Bible, and founded schools, workshops and a training college. They also grew coffee and some of the first cocoa in the country. The Presbyterian Church of Ghana grew from the mission. Its schools trained many of the clerks, teachers and nationalists of the Gold Coast. See also Christianity.
